content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
are the chemical "opposites" of acids. They neutralise acids and have their own distinctive properties. Understanding the relationship between bases and alkalis is crucial for chemistry.
A substance that neutralises an acid, typically by accepting H⁺ ions or providing O²⁻/OH⁻ ions.
A base that dissolves in water to produce hydroxide ions (OH⁻).
All alkalis are bases, but NOT all bases are alkalis.
Turn litmus blue, universal indicator blue/purple
More OH⁻ ions = more alkaline = higher pH
OH⁻ ions react with H⁺ ions: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O
This is the basis of neutralisation
Ammonia is a weak alkali (equilibrium lies to the left)
Can cause severe burns to skin and eyes
More dangerous to eyes than many acids
Wash any contact immediately with lots of water
Classify each substance as a base, an alkali, or both: NaOH, CuO, KOH, MgO, NH₃(aq)
Base only (neutralises acids but doesn't dissolve)
Explain why copper oxide is a base but not an alkali.
Copper oxide (CuO) is a base because it neutralises acids
However, copper oxide does not dissolve in water
It cannot produce OH⁻ ions in solution
Therefore, it is not an alkali
To be an alkali, a base must dissolve and produce OH⁻ ions
Write the equation showing how potassium hydroxide dissolves in water.
The OH⁻ ions make the solution alkaline.
Alkalis react with fats and oils in the skin
This is why you should wash hands after contact - the alkali is reacting with your skin!
Strong alkalis can cause serious burns this way
Only bases that DISSOLVE in water are alkalis
Thinking alkalis are less dangerous than acids
Strong alkalis can be more damaging, especially to eyes
Writing the formula of calcium hydroxide as CaOH
It's Ca(OH)₂ because calcium has 2+ charge
Neutralises acids (includes metal oxides and hydroxides)
A base that dissolves in water, producing OH⁻ ions
All alkalis are bases; not all bases are alkalis
Properties of alkalis: pH > 7, turn litmus blue, soapy feel, corrosive
Safety: Alkalis are corrosive - wear goggles and gloves
